harvestMonths.region: Eastern & Western Cape (main soft citrus areas) — Satsuma cultivars

evidence.quote: Miho Wase is also the cultivar that matures the earliest of the Satsuma cultivars, and can be harvested from as early as mid-March. Other Satsuma cultivars are harvested until around the end of May.
evidence.doc: Citrus Growers' Association / Citrus Academy — 'Citrus Planting Management 2: Citrus Types and Cultivars' Learner Guide (1st edition), Citrus Resource Warehouse (crw.org.za), citing CRI Cultivar Fact Sheets

harvestMonths.notes: Miho Wase is stated to be '85% of satsuma production'. Source: 'Still, 75% of soft citrus in southern Africa is planted in the Eastern and Western Cape.'

harvestMonths.region: Eastern & Western Cape (main soft citrus areas) — Clementine cultivars

evidence.quote: The earliest commercial clementine cultivar mature towards the end of March, with the last one finishing around mid-June.
evidence.doc: Citrus Growers' Association / Citrus Academy — 'Citrus Planting Management 2: Citrus Types and Cultivars' Learner Guide (1st edition), citing CRI Cultivar Fact Sheets

harvestMonths.notes: Nules is 'the most popular clementine cultivar ... about 75% of planted hectares' per the same source.

harvestMonths.region: Eastern & Western Cape (main soft citrus areas) — Mandarin cultivars (incl. Nadorcott)

evidence.quote: Nadorcott is the most common mandarin cultivar, and accounts for about two thirds of the hectares planted with mandarin cultivars. Early mandarin cultivars are ready to be harvested around mid-May, and the season from there stretches as late as September.
evidence.doc: Citrus Growers' Association / Citrus Academy — 'Citrus Planting Management 2: Citrus Types and Cultivars' Learner Guide (1st edition), citing CRI Cultivar Fact Sheets

harvestMonths.notes: 'Novas' and 'minneolas' are separately noted as marketed under the mandarin umbrella but are technically distinct hybrids (Nova harvested April-mid-June; minneola mid-May-end of July) — not included in the months above since they are not Citrus reticulata proper.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: Not found for soft citrus specifically. The KwaZulu-Natal DARD 'Fruit and Nut Production in KZN' guide gives a 'First crop (years)' table but only for Valencias/Navels/Grapefruit/Lemons — soft citrus/mandarins are not included in that table.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: Not found for soft citrus specifically in any source checked.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Not found. The CRW 'Citrus Types and Cultivars' learner guide has only a qualitative rootstock-comparison rating ('Yield per tree: High/Good') with no kg figures, and the KZN DARD yields table (tons/ha with first-crop years) does not include soft citrus/mandarins.

evidence.quote: Soft citrus/Mandarins – Base temperature 10oC. HU 1 600 to 2 200 (Jan – Apr: 1 000 – 1 250).
evidence.doc: KwaZulu-Natal Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, 'Fruit and Nut Production in KZN' (Horticultural Advisory Notes)

chillUnits.notes: This is a heat-unit (HU, base 10°C) requirement for fruit development, not a classic winter chill-unit/chill-hour requirement. No source found gave an explicit chill-unit figure or an explicit 'no chill requirement' statement for soft citrus, so left null; the HU figure is preserved here as the closest sourced analogue (evergreen citrus dormancy/flowering is driven by heat-unit accumulation and moisture/cold stress rather than a deciduous-style chilling model).

pollination.notes: Set to null in editor review: the quote says 'Nadorcott' is self-incompatible, which contradicts 'self-fertile'; seedless fruit set without pollination is parthenocarpy, and no enum value states it. Withdrawn value: self-fertile.

gaps: Years to first crop, years to full bearing, and per-tree yield (kg) not found for soft citrus/mandarins in any source checked (the one SA yields table located, from KZN DARD, covers Valencias/Navels/Grapefruit/Lemons only, not soft citrus).
No classic chill-unit/chill-hour figure found; only a heat-unit (HU) figure for fruit maturation.
